title: A backup of the house folder
summary: Second copy on a USB you already have, or another old PC. rsync. RAID is not a backup.

start.body: The share is useful the day that computer dies only if a second copy exists. That second copy is a backup. Tool: rsync — already on Debian and Ubuntu.

choices.label: Another old PC on the house network

usb.body: Plug the disk in. Find it with lsblk (often /dev/sdb1 — use what lsblk prints). Mount: sudo mkdir -p /mnt/backup && sudo mount /dev/sdb1 /mnt/backup. Then: rsync -a /srv/share/ /mnt/backup/share/ — trailing slashes matter.

other-pc.body: If SSH already works on the second box: rsync -a /srv/share/ otheruser@other-address:share-backup/. Trailing slashes still matter.

after.body: Confirm files landed before you trust it. USB path: sudo umount /mnt/backup, then leave the disk unplugged most of the time. Same command next week — rsync only copies what changed.

photos-ask.body: Phone photos are a different pile. Interested in a real photo backup later — Immich, Prism, or neither for now?

choices.label: Yeah — mark me interested in photos

photos-pick.body: Two common paths. Immich is the full Google-Photos-shaped stack. Prism is lighter. Pick a direction or leave it for later.

pick-immich.body: Noted. When you are ready, run Immich: first weekend. Docker on the lab box, phone app pointed at your LAN.

pick-prism.body: Noted. Prism intro is a short stub when you want it — same idea, less surface area.

done.body: Folder backup is enough for today. Come back when photos start to itch.
